text:
Tech-West England Advocates (TWEA) is the West of England group of the Global Tech Advocates (GTA) network, founded by Richard Lowe. It is a not-for-profit, volunteer-led community that supports tech founders and scale-ups across the West of England, the South West and the West Midlands, and connects them with partners, investors and international markets.
What we do: events and founder clinics; international trade missions; sector ambassadors; and a quarterly newsletter. Partners have included DSIT/the Department for Business and Trade, the University of the West of England, UK Tech Advocates and Tech London Advocates & Global Tech Advocates.
2027 priorities: stronger support for regional and UK scale-ups, and connecting more capital to ambitious founders, especially at Series A and beyond, through the GTA Innovation Funding Working Group.
Founder skills we want to fund: pitching and investment readiness, practical AI and automation, international growth, and fair access for under-represented founders.
Contact: contact@techwestenglandadvocates.co.uk
Organisation: a not-for-profit. Like all Tech Advocates networks, TWEA has a sole Founder and a group of volunteer Ambassadors, run in a more structured way than most.
Income: very small at present, so not a headline in bids.
Plan for 2027: commercialise more by bringing in more funding and sponsorship.
Where we are now: moving into a new phase, having built credibility through our events and trade missions. In 2027 TWEA will professionalise its volunteer Ambassador roles with clear expectations; a welcome pack for Ambassadors is being shared in December 2026.
voice: Warm, confident and practical. UK English. Celebrate founders by name, but only with their consent. Short sentences, and no hype words like "revolutionary". One clear call to action. 2–4 hashtags on LinkedIn.
